Definition: to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make a show, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses hâlal where we would say to praise, to boast, to shine. In Genesis 12:15, the text says "The princes also of Pharaoh saw her." In Judges 16:24, the text says "they praised their god."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading hâlal this way, I believe worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Abram in Egypt; Absalom Returns to Jerusalem
